events.reason: Resolving the disagreement between the two prior reports: report 1 correctly created a new family (family-generative-falsification-languages-control) because this submission's delivered capability (a same-text nine-language cross-linguistic morphology sweep) is not the Cardan table-and-grille mechanism experiment nor any other occupied family's scope; it only shares the metric suite and Voynich baseline as inputs, which per CREDIT_IS_NOT_LINEAGE_V1 does not bind it into family-generative-falsification's ladder despite the contributor's own 'extends' declaration. Report 2 incorrectly folded it into family-generative-falsification as an 'extension,' relying on the contributor's declared family_id and treating it as analogous in kind to poetry-control/controls-entry-ladder (which are themselves separately registered families, not sub-ladder entries of family-generative-falsification) -- this is the FAMILY_IDENTITY_GUARD_V1 error the methodology warns against: a claimant-supplied family_id is not binding, and the existing family-generative-falsification scope (Cardan grille mechanism) does not cover a no-mechanism, real-language control. This is a genuinely useful bounded diagnostic (one new axis: cross-linguistic morphology) answering one named objection with a disconfirming counter-example (Russian), structurally analogous to the already-independently-registered poetry-control and controls-entry-ladder families, each assessed at tier 2 for a single fixed metric suite applied across one systematic sweep. It does not meet tier 5's 'informative controlled pilot' threshold as a fully new reusable capability since it reuses the pre-existing metric suite/baseline verbatim and 7/9 language rows are not independently inspectable from supplied bytes (reference_only). Award tier 2.

families_added.scope: A bounded diagnostic control extending the generative-falsification metric suite (final-glyph entropy, conditional bigram entropy H2|1, type/token diversity, word length) to nine same-text (Bible) translations at equal 35k-token samples, testing whether a morphologically rich real language naturally reproduces the manuscript's word-ending discipline. Finds no tested language reaches the manuscript on either final-glyph entropy or H2|1; Finnish is nearest on endings (2.80 vs 2.58) but not close on H2|1; Russian, despite rich inflection, has the least predictable endings, refuting a simple morphology-based explanation; manuscript retains highest type diversity of all ten texts.
families_added.acceptance_test: Run `python languages_control.py --corpus ../../data/corpora/ZL3b-n.txt --bibles <dir with the nine bible-corpus XMLs> --out results/`; confirm results.json matches the recorded output showing every language's word-final entropy above the manuscript's 2.585 (nearest Finnish 2.803) and every language's H2|1 above 2.261 (nearest Greek 3.143), with manuscript ttr (0.2893) highest among all ten texts; independently reproduce the Latin and English-WEB rows from the two committed corpora.
excluded_overlap: Does not claim or extend the Cardan table-and-grille (M5a/M5b) mechanism experiment credited under family-generative-falsification.
Does not claim the rhyme/versification line-structure control credited under family-generative-falsification-poetry-control.
Does not claim the entry-structure genre-ladder metrics credited under family-generative-falsification-controls-entry-ladder.
Does not claim credit for the pinned ZL3b corpus/parser (seed-corpus-parser) or local harness workflow (seed-local-harness), used only as inputs.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: Pilot 4 in the generative-mechanism falsification family: implements the Cardan table-and-grille device (M5a independent-column, M5b row-coupled) built from the pinned ZL3b corpus, measures composite distance against real manuscript statistics across 28 configurations plus multi-seed stability, and narrows the residual gap to two local metrics (conditional bigram entropy, word-final predictability), extending outcome-m4-template-doodler-pilot.
family_comparisons.reason: That family credits a specific generative mechanism (Cardan grille device) experiment; this submission tests no generative mechanism at all, instead testing real natural languages against the manuscript on entropy/diversity metrics. Different capability/result; only shares the metric suite and corpus as inputs, which per credit-is-not-lineage guidance does not bind it into that family.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: A new bounded diagnostic control in the generative-falsification research area: measures line-structured metrics (word-final char entropy, line-final word final-char entropy, line-initial first-char entropy, top-5 line-final word rhyme concentration) across the pinned ZL3b corpus's real lines, a newly added rhymed-verse control (Shakespeare's Sonnets, PG 1041), and existing Culpeper/Alice prose pseudo-line baselines, showing that rhyme (even at its most ending-constrained, 3.50 bits) does not approach the manuscript's every-word final-char entropy (2.59 bits), excluding versification as the mechanism behind the residual word-ending discipline, plus a side finding that the manuscript's line-final position is less constrained than its average word (2.99 vs 2.59), opposite of rhyme.
family_comparisons.reason: Poetry-control excludes versification via rhyme-structure metrics on English/prose baselines; this submission excludes morphology via a nine-language same-text sweep with a different corpus (bible-corpus) and different metric focus (final-glyph entropy/H2|1/diversity across languages, not line-structure). Both are same-style bounded controls answering distinct named objections but neither's scope covers the other's actual delivered result.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: A bounded diagnostic control extending the existing entry-structure metric suite (entry-private vocabulary share, adjacent/distant page Jaccard, ttr, entry token length) to two new real-text genres (Devil's Dictionary, Wonder Book of Knowledge) alongside the previously measured Culpeper/Alice controls, showing the manuscript's entry-private vocabulary is genre- and entry-length-dependent and lies on a continuum with short-entry real genres rather than being an order-of-magnitude outlier, with a documented correction to an earlier interpretive emphasis about device-overshoot.
family_comparisons.reason: Entry-ladder tests entry-structure/genre metrics on English-genre texts; this submission tests cross-language morphology on Bible translations with entropy/diversity metrics. Different axis, different corpus, different named objection answered.

If the contributor believes the multilingual control constitutes a reusable checked capability meeting tier 5 (e.g., a general same-text cross-language control harness extensible to further objections with more committed-byte language corpora), they may resubmit with evidence of that broader reusability for reassessment.
assessment.appeal_route: Reply on the PR citing the specific gate or family-comparison the contributor disputes, with pointers to the exact evidence paths; a fresh assessment stage may be triggered per the effective methodology if material new evidence or context is supplied. Disputes about family-boundary judgment should reference the acceptance-test text of the family the contributor believes applies, and should address why the delivered result (not the declared family_id or 'extends' link) matches that family's existing scope.
